chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad bin Sinan, from al-Husayn bin Mukharrq, from Zaid al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding His saying: «The blemish of a believer upon another believer is forbidden», that he said: It is not that he is uncovered and something of him is seen. It is only that something bad is narrated about him.

key_terms.عَوْرَة: Blemish; private parts; that which is covered or hidden
key_terms.يَنْكَشِف: To be uncovered; to be revealed
key_terms.يُرْوَى عَلَيْهِ: To be narrated about him; to have something said about him

ai.seo_question: What does 'the blemish of a believer is forbidden' mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this interpretation from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), shifting the focus from physical modesty (*awrah*) to the moral sanctity of a believer's reputation. The Imam clarifies that the 'forbidden blemish' refers to exposing a person's faults through narration or backbiting, a concept central to Shia ethics regarding social conduct. This distinction highlights the importance of guarding one's speech to preserve the dignity of fellow believers.
